assertions.text: Tests use @pytest.mark.parametrize (or pytest.param rows) — not one test function per case, and not a loop over cases inside a single test body.
Parametrized cases carry scenario identifiers — an ids= argument or pytest.param(..., id=...) — so each case has a readable name in test output.
assertions.evidence: Parametrized cases carry ids (ids= or pytest.param id=)

assertions.text: Test function bodies contain no if/elif statements — expected outcomes come from the parametrized data, not branching logic.
assertions.evidence: No if/elif statements in test function bodies

assertions.text: Policy thresholds (age 70, 90-day trip limit) appear as explicit values in the test data alongside the applicant's actual values, making the comparison visible to the reader — not only baked invisibly into which cases were chosen.
assertions.evidence: Thresholds (70, 90) are implicit in test selection but never appear as explicit columns. E.g., row 'age_boundary_70' shows age=70 but threshold 70 is not visible as a separate column.

assertions.text: Scenario ids describe conditions ('senior without clearance', 'trip just over limit') — not outcomes ('approved', 'declined').
assertions.evidence: IDs end with outcomes: '...approved', '...declined', '...manual_review'. E.g., 'age_boundary_70-trip_boundary_90-no_clearance-declined' ends with outcome.

assertions.text: Parametrize argument names use domain language (age, trip_days, decision) — not generic names like a, b, val1, expected1.
assertions.evidence: 'age, trip_days, destination_restricted, has_medical_clearance, expected' are all domain-specific language terms.

assertions.text: Case values use concrete domain values (73, 91, Decision.APPROVED) — not abstract placeholders like 'CATEGORY_A' or magic sentinel numbers with no domain meaning.
assertions.evidence: All values are concrete: 'pytest.param(75, 30, False, True, Decision.APPROVED, ...)' uses actual ages, days, and Decision enum.

assertions.text: Multiple parametrized tests are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: Single parametrized test covers all 16 cases: '@pytest.mark.parametrize' with one CASES list mixing age/clearance, trip duration, and destination rules.

assertions.text: Each parametrized test has only the cases needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer cases per test is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: 16 cases in single test; combining concerns creates permutations. E.g., restricted_destination tested with multiple age/trip combinations rather than separated.

assertions.text: Age/clearance policy, trip-duration policy, and destination restriction are separated into distinct parametrized tests, rather than every rule exercised through one combined table.
assertions.evidence: All rules tested in one '@pytest.mark.parametrize' block. No separate test_age_clearance, test_trip_duration, test_destination tests.

assertions.text: Rule precedence is visible from concrete cases: a restricted destination with an otherwise approvable profile is DECLINED, and a >90-day trip is MANUAL_REVIEW even when the age/clearance rule alone would decline or approve.
assertions.evidence: Cases show precedence: 'pytest.param(75, 30, True, True, Decision.DECLINED, ...)' (destination overrides approval) and 'pytest.param(75, 120, False, True, Decision.MANUAL_REVIEW, ...)' (trip >90 days overrides age+clearance approval).

assertions.text: The effect of medical clearance for applicants aged 70+ is visible from paired cases: the same senior profile appears with clearance (APPROVED) and without (DECLINED). The clearance parameter's effect must be readable from the rows, not just implied.
assertions.evidence: Paired cases at age 75, 30 days: 'pytest.param(75, 30, False, True, Decision.APPROVED, ...)' and 'pytest.param(75, 30, False, False, Decision.DECLINED, ...)' show clearance effect directly.

assertions.text: pytest can import and collect the test modules against the project scaffolding
